title: Kernel gating and cost-model synthesis for on-the-fly kernel selection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a lightweight kernel-gating layer plus a synthesized cost model that combines offline microbenchmark matrices with online telemetry to pick the best kernel variant at request time. This ticket covers: (1) kernel gating API in the runtime that exposes features (arch, seqlen, batch_size, dtype, prefix-cache-hit, quant-level), (2) cost-model synthesis algorithm that fuses static microbenchmarks and exponential-moving-average telemetry weights, (3) integration with prefill/decode scheduler to allow different kernels at prefill vs decode phases, and (4) safe rollout + telemetry+canary hooks for continuous calibration.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha: Initial problem statement and trade-offs. We need a single decision point in the runtime to avoid scattered heuristics; prefer a synthesized cost function rather than large lookup tables to keep memory small on CPU control plane.

2026-02-24 - Tomás: Prototype gating design: small decision tree with fallback to 'best-known' kernel; want to replace tree with a linear gating model once we have telemetry. Posting microbenchmark harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124

2026-02-28 - Eng Review (Mina Chen): Concern about operator switching overhead during decode - might increase p95. Suggest measuring kernel switch cost and bounding it with hysteresis on consecutive tokens before switching during decode.

2026-03-03 - Tomás: Ran A100/H100 microbenchmarks for 4 quantization levels and 3 seqlen ranges. Results uploaded to dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference.com/d/bench/kernel-gating-matrix. Observed that for seqlen<=64 small-kernel wins on A100 at batch 1, but H100 prefers fused kernel at seqlen 64-128. Added results to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/Kernel+Gating+Design
2026-03-06 - Ops (Lena Patel): Canary plan approved. We'll route 5% traffic to new gating path, with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases by >12% or error rate increases >0.5%.

2026-03-10 - Tomás: Implemented cost-model synthesis. Early validation on synthetic seqlen distribution reduces average cost (tokens/sec normalized) by ~7% vs static policy without increasing p95. Need follow-up to test with live workload distributions and RBAC for private deploys. Created implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3251
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a single kernel_gating hook accepting a standardized feature vector (arch, seqlen_bucket, batch_size, dtype, quant, cache_hit)
Cost-model synthesizer merges offline microbenchmark table with online telemetry weights and exposes a REST/GRPC endpoint for debug readout
Prefill and decode scheduler obey gating decisions; switching hysteresis prevents token-level oscillation during decode
Canary route shows no >12% regression in p95 or >0.5% increase in error rate for 24h in production at 5% traffic
End-to-end tests (microbench harness + synthetic distributions) included in CI and run on A100/H100/MI300 matrix
